senses.gloss: मधव्य मधव्य. See p. 734, col. 1.

मधव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, fitted or authorized to
drink Soma; consisting of Soma; sweet; (अस्), m.
= Mādhava, the second month of spring.

माधव्य, अस्, m. a patronymic from Madhu,
see Pāṇ. IV. 1, 106.

मधु मधु, उस्, उस् or ऊस् or वी, उ (connected
with rt. 2. मद्, but in Uṇādi-s. 1. 19. said to be fr.
rt. मन्; for declension of neut. see Gram. 115; in
Ved. the gen. of the neut. may be मधोस्, inst.
मध्वा, loc. मधौ, fem. nom. pl. मध्वीस्),
sweet, of a pleasant taste or flavour, pleasant, agree-
able; (उ), n. anything sweet (especially if liquid),
mead; Soma (सोम्यम् मधु, Ṛg-veda 1. 19, 9);
honey (said to possess intoxicating qualities and to be
of eight kinds); milk or anything produced from
milk (as butter, melted butter, ghee, Ved.); the juice
or nectar of flowers, any sweet intoxicating drink,
wine, spirituous liquor; sugar; sweetness; water;
N. of one of the Brāhmaṇas; a particular metre,
four times ˘˘; (उस्), m., N. of the first month of
the year, = Caitra (March-April); the spring; Bassia
Latifolia; Jonesia Asoka; liquorice (= मधूक,
मधु-द्रुम); N. of an Asura or Daitya (gene-
rally associated with Kaiṭabha and along with him
slain by Viṣṇu); N. of another Asura (father of the
Rākṣasa Lavaṇa and killed in Madhu-vana by
Śatru-ghna, who founded there the city of Mathurā
or Madhurā; this Asura is sometimes identified with
the previous one); N. of a son of the third Manu;
of one of the seven sages under Manu Cākṣuṣa;
of various princes, of a son of Vṛṣa, of Deva-
kṣatra, of Bindumat, of Arjuna Kārtavīrya; N. of
a teacher [cf. मध्व]; N. of a mountain; (अवस्),
m. pl. the race of Madhu, = the Yādavas or Mā-
thuras; (उस्), f. a particular plant, = Jīvā or Jīvantī;
[cf. Zend madhu, ‘honey;’ Gr. μέθ-υ, μεθ-ύ-ω,
μεθ-ύ-σκ-ω, μέλι in which θ or δ is changed into λ;
Lat. mel, mellis for melvis = meduis (?); Angl. Sax.
med-u, med-o; Old Germ. met-o, medu; Slav.
med-ŭ; Lith. mid-u-s, ‘honey;’ Hib. mil, gen.
meala, ‘honey.’]

girl arrived at puberty, a marriageable woman; N.
of the second or middle Grantha of the Kāṭhaka.
—मध्यमक-वृत्ति or मध्यमिक-वृत्ति,
इस्, f., N. of a book.
—मध्यमकालङ्कार (˚क-

—मध्य-
मकालोक (˚क-आल्˚), अस्, m., N. of a Buddhist
work.
मध्यमकेय, आस्, m. pl., N. of a people.

माध्यमकेय, आस्, m. pl., N. of a people, =
मध्यमकेय.

मध्यमिक, आस्, m. pl., N. of a school of
Buddhists, the followers of Nāgārjuna.

माध्यमिक, अस्, ई, अम्, relating or belonging
to the middle, middlemost, middle; (आस्), m. pl.,
N. of a Buddhist school; of a people in the central
part of India.

मध्यमीय, अस्, आ, अम्, middlemost, middle,
central.

मध्व मध्व, अस्, m., N. of the founder of
a sect of Vaiṣṇavas in the south of India in the
thirteenth century, hence called the Mādhava sect,
(his N. was properly Ānanda-tīrtha Bhagavat-pāda,
he is also called Madhu.)
—मध्व-गुरु, उस्, or
मध्वाचार्य (˚व-आच्˚), अस्, m. = मध्व above.
—मध्व-मुख-भङ्ग, अस्, m. or मध्व-
मुख-मर्दन, अम्, n. ‘the bruising of the face
of Madhva,’ N. of a work by Appi Dīkṣita refuting
Madhva's notions respecting the Vedānta.
—म-
ध्वाचार्य-विजय, अस्, m., N. of a book.

1. माध्व, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. मधु), sweet; (ई),
f. a kind of spirituous liquor; = माधवी, Gærtnera
Racemosa; = माधुर-कण्टक, a kind of fish;
(ई), m. du., Ved. ‘possessing or loving sweetness,’ an
epithet of the Aśvins; (Sāy.) = मधु-पूर्ण-पात्र-
युक्तौ; (in this last sense perhaps fr. a base मा-
ध्वि.)
—माध्वी-मधुरा, f. a species of date
(= मधुर-खर्जुरिका).

माध्व 2. माध्व, अस्, m. (for 1. see col. 2),
an adherent of Madhva.

मध्वक्ष मध्व्-अक्ष, &c. See p. 738,
col. 1.

माधव माधव, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. मधु), made
of honey, honey-like, sweet; relating to spring,
vernal; belonging or peculiar to the descendants
of Madhu, i. e. the Yādavas, (माधवे ऽहनि, on a
spring day; माधवी लक्ष्मीः, vernal beauty or,
in Hari-vaṃśa 9597, the fortune of the Yādavas;
माधवी देवी, N. of the earth); (अस्), m. an epithet
of the second month of spring; the month Vai-
śākha (= April-May); spring; a son or descendant
of Madhu, a man of the race of Yadu; an epithet of
Kṛṣṇa (Viṣṇu); of Paraśu-rāma (as an incarnation
of Viṣṇu); of Indra; of a son of the third Manu;
of one of the seven sages under Manu Bhautya; of
another ancient sage; of a leader of the Pañca-rātra
sect; of the author of the Rug-viniścaya; of the
father of Dādābhāī and grandfather of the astrological
writer Nārāyaṇa; of the father of the commentator
Someśvara; of various other persons; Bassia Lati-
folia or a species of leguminous plant, = कृष्ण-
मुद्ग; (ई), f. honey-sugar, clayed or candied sugar;
an intoxicating drink made of honey, mead; ‘spring-
flower,’ Gærtnera Racemosa [cf. वासन्ती]; a kind
of panic-grass; sacred basil; = मिसि (according to
some, a sort of dentifrice); a procuress, bawd; afflu-
ence in cattle or herds; a woman of the race of
Madhu or Yadu (e. g. An-antā, wife of Janam-ejaya;
Sampriyā, wife of Vidūratha; Kuntī, wife of Pāṇḍu);
N. of Dākṣāyaṇī in Śrī-śaila; of Durgā; of a
Mātṛ attending on Skanda; of a daughter of Yayāti;
of a commentary (probably named after the author
Mādhava); (अम्), n. sweetness; (in Schol. on Pāṇ.
IV. 4, 129, a fem. form माधवा is given, agreeing
with तनूः.)
—माधव-कर, अस्, m., N. of a
medical writer.
—माधव-काल-निर्णय, अस्, m.,
N. of a work written by Mādhavācārya.

nātha, q. q. v. v., (he is sometimes called simply Mā-
dhava, and regarded, together with Sāyaṇa, as, author

—माधवी-वन, अम्, n., N. of a

—माधवेन्द्र-पुरी (˚व-इन्˚), m., N. of

—माधवेष्टा (˚व-इष्˚), f. a species

—माधवोचित (˚व-उच्˚), अम्, n. a kind

माधवीय, अस्, आ, अम्, relating or belonging or
devoted to Mādhava or to Mādhavācārya; composed
by him.
—माधवीय-धातु-वृत्ति, इस्, f., N. of a

brother Mādhava).
—माधवीय-वेदार्थ-प्र-

माध्विक, अस्, m. a person who collects honey.

माध्वीक, अम्, n. a kind of intoxicating drink
distilled from the blossoms of the Bassia Latifolia;
wine, spirit distilled from grapes; [cf. मधु-म्˚.]
—माध्वीक-फल, अस्, n. a species of cocoa-nut
(= मधु-नालिकेरक).

माधुकर माधुकर, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. मधु-
कर), coming from a bee or from honey, belonging
to a bee, resembling a bee, (माधुकरी वृत्तिः, a
mode or course of life resembling that of a bee), be-
longing to honey, &c.; (ई), f. gathering alms after the
manner of a bee by going from door to door; alms
obtained from five different places by the third class
of religious mendicants.

माधूकर, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. मधु-कर),
gathered or collected after the manner of bees.

माधुकर्णिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. मधु-कर्ण),
see Gaṇa Kumudādi 2. to Pāṇ. IV. 2, 80.

दस्), Ved. relating to or coming from Madhu-cchan-
das; (अस्), m. a patronymic of Agha-marṣaṇa; of
Jetṛ.

माधुपर्किक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. मधु-पर्क),
relating to the Madhu-parka; offered or presented
as a token of respect to a guest.

माधुमत, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. मधु-मत्), be-
longing to or descended from Madhu-mat; (आस्), m.
pl. the inhabitants of Kaśmīra; belonging to the
river Madhu-matī, (माधुमतं जलम्, water
from the Madhu-matī.)

माधुमतक (fr. मधु-मत्), see Gaṇa Kac-
chādi to Pāṇ. IV. 2, 134.

माधुर्य, अस्, आ or -री (?), अम् (fr. मधुर),
speaking sweetly or kindly; (अम्), n. sweetness,
pleasantness, attractiveness, gracefulness; kindness,
friendliness, amiability; (in rhetoric) the succession
of single words in a sentence.

माधूची माधूची, m. du., Ved. (probably
formed after the analogy of माध्वी, see under
1. माध्व, col. 2), an epithet of the Aśvins.

माध्यन्दिन, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. मध्यन्-दिन),
Ved. belonging to midday, meridional, midday,
(माध्यन्दिने सवने, at the midday rite); middle,
central; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a branch of the Vājasa-
neyins and of an astronomical school who fixed the
starting-point of planetary movements at noon; (अम्),
n., scil. तीर्थ, N. of a Tīrtha; [cf. माध्यन्दि-
नीयक.]
—माध्यन्दिन-युग, Ved. belonging
to the midday oblation.
—माध्यन्दिन-शाखा, f.
the school of the Mādhyandinas.

मध्यन्-दिन; for ‘Puṣpa-pārṇa’ read पुष्-
पार्ण.

माध्यन्दिनायन, अस्, m. probably a patro-
nymic, N. of a preceptor.

माध्यन्दिनि, इस्, m. a patronymic, N. of a
grammarian.

माध्यन्दिनीय, अस्, आ, अम्, usual or customary
at the midday oblation (Ved.); ‘belonging to the
school of the Mādhyandinas,’ an epithet of Nārā-
yaṇa.
माध्यन्दिनीयक, अम्, n., N. of a Tīrtha.
माध्यन्दिनेय = माध्यन्दिन, q. v.

माध्यमस्थ्य, अम्, n. (fr. मध्यम-स्थ),
the state of standing or being in the middle, see
Gaṇa Brāhmaṇādi to Pāṇ. V. 1, 124; [cf. मा-
ध्यस्थ्य.]

माध्यमिनेय, अस्, m. (fr. मध्यमा), a
metronymic, see Gaṇa Kalyāṇyādi to Pāṇ. IV. 1,
126.

माध्यस्थ माध्यस्थ, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. मध्य-
स्थ), being in a middle state, indifferent, impartial,
neutral; (अम्), n. middle state or condition; indif-
ference, impartiality.

माध्यस्थ्य, अम्, n. ‘the state of standing in
the middle or between two,’ indifference, impartiality,
neutrality; the office of umpire, mediation, inter-
cession.

माध्याह्निक माध्याह्निक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr.
मध्याह्न), belonging to midday, taking place
at noon.
मधु-वन; after ‘cuckoo’ insert (अम्), n.
